final.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
final.body:
If an AI tool has to look things up to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow design. When the system searches documents, emails, FAQs, or past records, it has to pull back the right material consistently, or the answer looks neat and is wrong. That creates rework, or a confident mistake. For a small business, the question is not “can AI answer this?” but “can it find the right source every time this task runs?”

The practical rule of thumb is simple: if one recurring task needs you to search more than one place for the answer, retrieval quality has become a design constraint. That could be customer questions, invoice checks, or lead follow-up. My next step would be to audit the source material for that one task: are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If the inputs are messy, automation usually moves the manual work earlier rather than removing it.

Bareni’s self-built local knowledge-assistant demo can show sources on synthetic data, but the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. The useful habit for an owner is still the same: before you automate a workflow, ask whether the information is organised well enough to retrieve.
